def score(f, p, hw, w):
    # Compress output-boundary overhang so very large edge tiles do not dominate.
    s = np.log2(1.0 + f.edge_waste) * w[0]
    # Final-wave underfill is a separate loss from fixed dispatch/startup cost.
    s = s + f.tail_waste * w[1]
    # Reverse the wave-deficit preference: a small grid has less amortization.
    s = s + f.wave_count_deficit * w[2]
    # Preserve both the qualitative spill event and its traffic severity.
    s = s + f.has_spill * w[3]
    s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.spill_traffic_ratio) * w[4]
    # Short reductions expose pipeline fill/drain and absolute loop-control work.
    s = s + f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction * w[5]
    s = s + f.pipeline_stage_family * w[6]
    s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.mainloop_iteration_count) * w[7]
    if p.output_work_per_sm < 256 or p.output_aspect_imbalance > 0.75 or p.log_min_dim < 7:
        # Sparse or skinny outputs are especially sensitive to tile geometry and thread amortization.
        s = s + f.tile_aspect_mismatch * w[8]
        s = s + f.thread_work_granularity_deficit * w[9]
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.edge_waste) * w[10]
        if p.roofline_ratio < 1:
            # In the memory-bound sparse regime, replicated operands and weak tile intensity cost bandwidth.
            s = s + np.log2(f.operand_tile_traffic_ratio) * w[11]
            s = s + f.tile_roofline_deficit * w[12]
            # Split-K is useful here when it supplies missing waves, but its partition count and reduction costs remain real.
            s = s + np.log2(f.split_k_slices) * w[36]
            s = s + f.wave_count_deficit * np.log2(f.split_k_slices) * w[37]
            s = s + f.wave_count_deficit * w[16]
            s = s + f.serial_reduction_dependency * w[17]
            s = s + f.parallel_reduction_traffic_fraction * w[18]
            s = s + f.parallel_reduction_compute_fraction * w[19]
        else:
            # In the compute-bound sparse regime, issue work and limited residency dominate.
            s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.instruction_density) * w[13]
            s = s + f.occupancy_deficit * w[14]
            s = s + f.resident_block_scarcity * w[15]
            # Extra split-K waves can help underfilled outputs, subject to serial and parallel reduction overhead.
            s = s + np.log2(f.split_k_slices) * w[38]
            s = s + f.wave_count_deficit * np.log2(f.split_k_slices) * w[39]
            s = s + f.wave_count_deficit * w[20]
            s = s + f.serial_reduction_dependency * w[21]
            s = s + f.parallel_reduction_traffic_fraction * w[22]
            s = s + f.parallel_reduction_compute_fraction * w[23]
    else:
        # Large rectangular saturated outputs form a distinct tile-selection regime.
        if p.output_aspect_imbalance > 0.75 and p.log_flops > 40:
            # Here the global wave preference is deliberately weakened so geometry and tail waste decide.
            s = s + f.wave_count_deficit * w[29]
            s = s + f.tail_waste * w[30]
            s = s + f.tile_aspect_mismatch * w[31]
            s = s + f.thread_work_granularity_deficit * w[32]
            s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.edge_waste) * w[33]
            # Resource cliffs are joint effects: pressure matters most when it also removes resident CTAs.
            s = s + f.shared_memory_pressure * f.resident_block_scarcity * w[34]
            s = s + f.register_file_pressure * f.resident_block_scarcity * w[35]
        else:
            # For other saturated outputs, select the appropriate memory or compute bottleneck without adding another path.
            s = s + np.where(p.roofline_ratio < 1, np.log2(f.operand_tile_traffic_ratio), 0.0) * w[24]
            s = s + np.where(p.roofline_ratio < 1, f.tile_roofline_deficit, 0.0) * w[25]
            s = s + np.where(p.roofline_ratio < 1, 0.0, np.log2(1.0 + f.instruction_density)) * w[26]
            s = s + np.where(p.roofline_ratio < 1, 0.0, f.occupancy_deficit) * w[27]
            s = s + np.where(p.roofline_ratio < 1, 0.0, f.resident_block_scarcity) * w[28]
            # Add the same joint allocation penalty in the saturated regime, where oversized row tiles create cliffs.
            s = s + f.shared_memory_pressure * f.resident_block_scarcity * w[34]
            s = s + f.register_file_pressure * f.resident_block_scarcity * w[35]
    return s

def score(f, p, hw, w):
    # Output-tile overhang: compress the wide edge-waste range.
    s = np.log2(1.0 + f.edge_waste) * w[0]
    # Any register spill introduces exceptionally expensive local-memory accesses.
    s = s + f.has_spill * w[1]
    s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.spill_traffic_ratio) * w[2]
    # A nearly empty final wave leaves a rapidly growing fraction of the GPU idle.
    s = s + (-np.log2(np.maximum(1.0e-6, 1.0 - f.tail_waste))) * w[3]
    # A one-wave or nearly one-wave grid also pays launch/dispatch startup and
    # fails to amortize grid scheduling, so wave deficit is an explicit penalty.
    s = s + f.wave_count_deficit * w[4]
    # Pipeline prologue/epilogue cost is poorly amortized by short reductions.
    s = s + f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction * w[5]
    # Serial split-K partitions introduce an accumulator dependency.
    s = s + f.serial_reduction_dependency * w[6]
    # The multistage family has a fixed family-level cost, especially when it is not amortized.
    s = s + f.multistage_family_indicator * w[15]
    s = s + f.multistage_family_indicator * f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction * w[16]
    # Long mainloops can amortize multistage setup and expose its steady-state advantage.
    s = s + f.multistage_family_indicator * np.log2(f.mainloop_iteration_count) * w[17]
    if p.roofline_ratio < 1.0:
        # In the bandwidth-bound regime, replicated operand loads dominate.
        s = s + np.log2(f.operand_tile_traffic_ratio) * w[7]
        # Low-intensity CTA tiles directly increase bandwidth pressure.
        s = s + f.tile_roofline_deficit * w[8]
        # Parallel split-K partials add global-memory traffic in this regime.
        s = s + f.parallel_reduction_traffic_fraction * w[9]
        # Traversal locality is a cache/geometry-sensitive proxy for the discrete
        # swizzle policy; expose both its baseline cost and its L2-pressure interaction.
        s = s + f.cta_traversal_locality_loss * w[20]
        s = s + f.cta_traversal_locality_loss * p.l2_working_set_pressure * w[21]
        # The discrete 2x2 swizzle transitions add a separate cache/TLB disruption cost.
        s = s + f.swizzle_neighborhood_discontinuity * w[22]
        s = s + f.swizzle_neighborhood_discontinuity * p.l2_working_set_pressure * w[23]
    else:
        # In the compute-bound regime, front-end instruction overhead is exposed.
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.instruction_density) * w[10]
        # Thread-slot underfill reduces latency hiding for arithmetic pipelines.
        s = s + f.occupancy_deficit * w[11]
        # Register allocation pressure limits concurrent latency-hiding CTAs.
        s = s + f.register_file_pressure * w[12]
        # Shared-memory allocation pressure limits CTA residency and buffering.
        s = s + f.shared_memory_pressure * w[13]
        # Parallel split-K reduction arithmetic adds compute work in this regime.
        s = s + f.parallel_reduction_compute_fraction * w[14]
        # Keep the discrete swizzle effect active even when traversal locality is
        # not used by the compute-bound model.
        s = s + f.swizzle_neighborhood_discontinuity * w[24]
        if p.log_min_dim > 8.0 and p.output_aspect_imbalance < 0.25:
            # For large, square compute-bound GEMMs, granularity is less harmful when
            # scarce residency is being used efficiently by a low-deficit tile.
            s = s + f.thread_work_granularity_deficit * (1.0 - f.resident_block_scarcity) * w[18]
            # Reward the complementary case: extra CTA scarcity is acceptable when
            # the tile has enough intra-CTA work to amortize its thread overhead.
            s = s + f.resident_block_scarcity * (1.0 - f.thread_work_granularity_deficit) * w[19]
    return s

    # Final-wave idle time grows sharply as the usable wave fraction vanishes.
    s = s + np.log2(1.0 / np.clip(1.0 - f.tail_waste, 1e-6, 1.0)) * w[1]
    # Register spilling introduces a severe local-memory latency penalty.
    s = s + f.has_spill * w[2]
    s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.spill_traffic_ratio) * w[3]
    # A large CTA footprint is costly when the shape's working set pressures L2.
    s = s + np.where(p.l2_working_set_pressure > 0.5,
                     np.log2(1.0 + f.cta_l2_footprint_ratio),
                     0.0) * w[23]
    # Misaligned shapes make the multistage async-copy family a compatibility risk.
    s = s + np.where(p.alignment_deficit > 0.25,
                     f.multistage_alignment_compatibility,
                     0.0) * w[24]
    # Extra pipeline state-machine groups impose a discrete control cost.
    s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.stage_family_control_cost) * w[25]
    # State-management cost is more exposed when shared memory limits residency.
    s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.stage_family_control_cost) * f.shared_memory_pressure * w[26]
    # Parallel split-K materialization adds global-memory traffic.
    s = s + f.parallel_reduction_traffic_fraction * w[20]
    # Parallel split-K also adds reduction arithmetic beyond ordinary accumulation.
    s = s + f.parallel_reduction_compute_fraction * w[21]
    # Fixed thread-level coordination is amortized by useful CTA output work.
    s = s + f.thread_work_granularity_deficit * w[22]
    if p.output_work_per_sm < 256:
        s = s + f.wave_count_deficit * w[4]
        s = s + f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction * w[5]
        s = s + np.log2(f.mainloop_iteration_count) * w[6]
        if p.roofline_ratio < 1:
            s = s + np.log2(f.operand_tile_traffic_ratio) * w[7]
            s = s + f.tile_roofline_deficit * w[8]
        else:
            s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.instruction_density) * w[9]
            s = s + f.occupancy_deficit * w[10]

    else:

        s = s + f.wave_count_deficit * (1.0 - f.serial_reduction_dependency) * w[12]

        s = s + f.serial_reduction_dependency * np.log2(f.mainloop_iteration_count) * w[28]

        s = s - np.log2(1.0 + f.split_k_independent_cta_load) * f.wave_count_deficit * (1.0 - f.serial_reduction_dependency) * w[40]

        if p.output_work_per_sm < 4096:
            s = s + np.where(p.roofline_ratio < 1,
                             np.log2(f.operand_tile_traffic_ratio),

            s = s + np.where(p.roofline_ratio < 1,

def score(f, p, hw, w):
    # Boundary overhang increases executed work; compress the wide edge-waste range.
    s = np.log2(1.0 + f.edge_waste) * w[0]
    # A register spill introduces very expensive local-memory traffic.
    s = s + f.has_spill * w[1]
    # Spill severity distinguishes a small spill from sustained local-memory traffic.
    s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.spill_traffic_ratio) * w[2]
    # A scarce CTA residency pool reduces latency hiding in every regime.
    s = s + f.resident_block_scarcity * w[3]
    if p.roofline_ratio < 1:
        # In the bandwidth-bound regime, replicated operand loads directly increase traffic.
        s = s + np.log2(f.operand_tile_traffic_ratio) * w[4]
        # Low tile arithmetic intensity adds pressure to the bandwidth bottleneck.
        s = s + f.tile_roofline_deficit * w[5]
        # Shared-memory allocation can reduce the resident CTA pool and buffering capacity.
        s = s + f.shared_memory_pressure * w[6]
        # Register allocation can independently reduce latency-hiding CTAs.
        s = s + f.register_file_pressure * w[7]
    else:
        # In the compute-bound regime, front-end instruction overhead competes with tensor issue.
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.instruction_density) * w[8]
        # Residual tile-level load pressure matters when cache reuse is poor, even above the shape roofline.
        s = s + (np.log2(f.operand_tile_traffic_ratio) / 20.0) * f.tile_roofline_deficit * p.l2_working_set_pressure * w[33]
        # Compute-bound kernels benefit from resources that hide execution latency.
        s = s + f.occupancy_deficit * w[9]
        # Register pressure directly limits concurrent compute CTAs and execution latency hiding.
        s = s + f.register_file_pressure * w[10]
        # Shared-memory pressure can constrain buffering and resident compute CTAs.
        s = s + f.shared_memory_pressure * w[11]
    # With little output work per SM, split-K can create useful CTA waves, but only
    # when its serial dependency does not erase that wave-creation benefit.
    if p.output_work_per_sm < 4096:
        reduction_scale = 1.0 + np.clip((p.log_flops - 20.0) / 20.0, 0.0, 1.0)
        s = s + f.wave_count_deficit * (1.0 - f.serial_reduction_dependency) * reduction_scale * w[12]
        # Serial split-K boundaries are a direct dependency cost, not a benefit.
        s = s + f.serial_reduction_dependency * w[13]
        s = s + f.parallel_reduction_traffic_fraction * w[14]
        s = s + f.parallel_reduction_compute_fraction * w[15]
        # Parallel reduction overhead is most harmful when there is little serial
        # dependency to avoid, so price traffic against the available serial benefit.
        s = s + f.parallel_reduction_traffic_fraction * (1.0 - f.serial_reduction_dependency) * w[34]
        s = s + f.parallel_reduction_compute_fraction * (1.0 - f.serial_reduction_dependency) * w[35]
    else:
        # Once output parallelism is ample, extra split-K waves are launch overhead
        # rather than a remedy, so all split-K effects are priced as costs.
        s = s + f.wave_count_deficit * w[16]
        s = s + f.serial_reduction_dependency * w[17]
        s = s + f.parallel_reduction_traffic_fraction * w[18]
        s = s + f.parallel_reduction_compute_fraction * w[19]
    # Swizzle exposure has a direct effect, but its sign and strength can change with geometry.
    s = s + f.swizzle_access_conflict_exposure * w[20]
    # Tile/output aspect mismatch changes whether exposed swizzle accesses are harmful.
    s = s + f.swizzle_access_conflict_exposure * (f.tile_aspect_mismatch / 20.0) * w[21]
    s = s + f.swizzle_access_conflict_exposure * p.output_aspect_imbalance * w[22]
    # With scarce residency, the same access exposure can alter scheduling and latency hiding.
    s = s + f.swizzle_access_conflict_exposure * f.resident_block_scarcity * w[23]
    # Rectangular outputs make aggregate boundary waste more informative about the short axis.
    s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.edge_waste) * p.output_aspect_imbalance * w[24]
    # A short output axis amplifies the cost of an imbalanced final CTA wave.
    s = s + f.tail_waste * p.output_aspect_imbalance * w[25]
    # Axis imbalance also makes insufficient CTA partitioning more costly than its scalar proxy suggests.
    s = s + f.wave_count_deficit * p.output_aspect_imbalance * w[26]
    # Narrow output-axis tiles amortize thread scheduling overhead less effectively.
    s = s + f.thread_work_granularity_deficit * p.output_aspect_imbalance * w[27]
    # Directional tile fit identifies axis-specific predication beyond scalar aspect measures.
    s = s + f.axis_tile_fit_imbalance * w[28]
    # The directional penalty is stronger when the output matrix is highly rectangular.
    s = s + f.axis_tile_fit_imbalance * p.output_aspect_imbalance * w[29]
    # Axis-specific tail waste compounds when the final wave is poorly filled.
    s = s + f.axis_tile_fit_imbalance * f.tail_waste * w[30]
    # Axis-specific tile fit matters more when the grid has a wave deficit.
    s = s + f.axis_tile_fit_imbalance * f.wave_count_deficit * w[31]
    # Directional predication and scarce resident CTAs jointly reduce useful scheduling choices.
    s = s + f.axis_tile_fit_imbalance * f.resident_block_scarcity * w[32]
    return s
